reading.body:
H.R. 6983, the PRICE Act, is a consumer energy bill that electric utilities have made their business, with 19 lobbying filings naming it.

The pattern is who showed up. Edison Electric Institute, the utility trade association, appears twice. The rest are utilities and generators: Portland General Electric, Puget Sound Energy, CMS Energy, Xcel Energy, FirstEnergy, PPL, Pinnacle West, American Electric Power. Google Client Services is the single non-utility filer. The bill's own text is tagged with energy and data centers, which is why it sits in an AI ecosystem index at all.

That matters because data center load growth is the demand curve utilities are now planning against. A bill about consumer rate inflation is where the question of who pays for new generation and transmission gets decided, and the filers are the parties who would carry or pass through those costs. The presence of one hyperscaler among ten utilities is the only direct signal that AI buyers are watching the same proceeding.

What the data does not say is what any of these filers want. A filing naming a bill shows the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken. There are no recorded votes in this set, no committee action, and no text of the bill itself, only a link to it. The sponsor and five cosponsors are all Democrats, which describes the bill's origin but not its prospects.

summary: H.R. 6983, PRICE Act Preventing Rate Inflation in Consumer Energy Act. Latest status date 2026-01-08. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: energy and data centers. 19 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
